name: Eventide-Barren
geological_features: Ancient lava plains cooled to smooth basalt
description: Eventide-Barren is a small, dead world whose geological activity ceased billions of years ago. Its surface is a testament to finality: smooth basalt lava plains that cooled into their present form when the planet's interior heat was finally exhausted, frozen in the moment of their last flow like a world caught at the end of its day.

The absence of atmosphere leaves the surface in stark binary: blinding light and absolute shadow, with no gradient between them. The dust in the low-gravity craters sits undisturbed, each particle in the position it settled into millennia ago, a stillness so complete it borders on eerie.

The graben systems that crack the basalt plains are the last testament to the planet's geological youth, stress fractures from a time when the interior still had enough heat to generate tectonic movement. They now serve only as traps for cosmic dust and as landmarks in an otherwise featureless landscape.

The titanium deposits in the basalt are the planet's primary commercial value, easily accessible on the weathering-free surface. Eventide-Barren serves as a reliable mining operation and emergency waystation, its predictability and emptiness a comfort to spacers who have seen too many hostile worlds.
